blocks.text: Modifying Zscaler Cloud Connectors and Cloud Connector groups is one of the tasks you can complete after deployment.
To edit a Cloud Connector or Cloud Connector group:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Cloud > Cloud Connector > Cloud Connector Groups.
Select the Overview or Upgrade Manager tab, depending on your requirements.
Locate the group or the individual connector you want to modify and click the Edit icon.
See image.
Cloud Connector group
In the Edit Cloud Connector Group window, view or configure the following:
On the Overview tab:
In the Auto Cleanup section, configure the following:
Auto Cleanup Frequency: Select the frequency at which Cloud Connector groups are automatically deleted (i.e., Never, 60 Days, 90 Days, or 120 Days).

Forced Delete: Select the checkbox to allow the deletion of Cloud Connectors, even if they are used by Internet & SaaS or Private Access traffic forwarding policies. If the deleted connector was the only location, the policy is bypassed. If not, the policy continues to apply to the remaining locations or Cloud Connector groups.
Auto Cleanup is in Limited Availability (LA). To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.
In the Global Profile section, configure the following:
Global Profile: From the drop-down menu, select a global profile. To learn more, see About Global Profiles.
Disaster Recovery Testing Mode: Select the checkbox to allow users to evaluate Disaster Recovery (DR) functionality without affecting production traffic.
In the Tunnel Information section, configure the following:
ZIA Tunnel Mode: Select Unencrypted UDP, DTLS, or TLS for the encryption type to be used when forwarding traffic to Internet & SaaS. By default, Unencrypted UDP is selected.

Fallback to TLS: You can only enable this feature if Unencrypted UDP or DTLS is selected as the ZIA Tunnel Mode. Select Enable to have the tunnel type automatically switch to TLS if the tunnel becomes unhealthy. Select Disable to deactivate this feature. This feature is enabled by default.
In the Group Information section, view the following:
Name: The name of the Cloud Connector group.
Location Name: The location from where your Cloud Connector was deployed.
No. of Connectors: The number of Cloud Connectors belonging to the Cloud Connector group.
Connector Names: The names of the Cloud Connectors.
See image.
On the Upgrade Status tab, configure the following:
In the Upgrade Schedule section, designate a Day and Time for periodic software updates. To learn more, see Managing Cloud & Branch Connector Upgrades.
In the Release Channel section, from the Choose release channel drop-down menu, select Stable, Latest, or Beta:
Stable: Select Stable to deploy your Cloud Connector on the channel that has been widely adopted and tested in real environments.
Latest: Select Latest to deploy your Cloud Connector on the channel that has the most recent production release.
Beta: Select Beta to deploy your Cloud Connector on the channel that has early access to new features and improvements. This channel might contain bugs and instability.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
Individual Cloud Connector
In the Edit Cloud Connector window:
On the Overview tab:
In the Operational Status section, configure or view the following:
Status: Select Enable or Disable to activate or disable the Cloud Connector.
Last Heartbeat Received On: View the date and time when the Zscaler service last received a heartbeat, or keepalive communication, from the Cloud Connector.
See image.
In the Tunnel Information section, view the following:
ZIA Tunnel Mode: View the encryption type to be used when forwarding traffic to Internet & SaaS. By default, Unencrypted UDP is selected.

Fallback to TLS: View the status of TLS fallback as Enable or Disable. If enabled, the tunnel type automatically switches to TLS if the tunnel becomes unhealthy. If disabled, this feature is deactivated. By default, TLS fallback is enabled.
See image.
In the Location Information section, view the following:
Name: The name of the Cloud Connector.
Location Name: The location where your Cloud Connector was deployed from.
Connector VM Size: The size of the Cloud Connector virtual machine (VM).
Provisioning Template Name: The name of the Cloud Connector provisioning template.
See image.
In the Connector Information section, view the following:
Management Outgoing Gateway IP Address: The default gateway IP address.
Management IP Address: The IP address of the Cloud Connector.
Management DNS Server 1: The IP address of the primary DNS server.
See image.
In the Forwarding Information section, view the following:
Internal Gateway IP Address: The gateway IP address.
DNS Server 1: The IP address of the primary DNS server.
See image.
In the Service Information section, view the following:
Service IP: The service IP address.
Virtual IP Address: The virtual IP address.
Load Balancer: The load balancer.
See image.
On the Upgrade Status tab:
In the Upgrade Schedule section, designate a Days and Time for periodic software updates. To learn more, see Managing Cloud & Branch Connector Upgrades.
In the Upgrade Information section, view the following:
Last Upgrade On: The last date and time the Cloud Connector was upgraded.
Current Version: The current version of the Cloud Connector.
Scheduled Version: The version scheduled to be applied when Cloud Connector upgrades next.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
